In June 2025, U.S. retail sales rebounded more than expected, rising by 0.6% after a 0.9% decrease in May, according to the Commerce Department's Census Bureau. This increase surpassed economists' forecasts, which had predicted a modest 0.1% uptick. However, analysts suggest that the rise may be partially attributed to price hikes on goods affected by tariffs rather than a genuine increase in consumer purchasing volumes. Specific categories like household furnishings, appliances, sporting goods, and toys saw notable price increases. Core retail sales, which exclude volatile components such as automobiles, gasoline, building materials, and food services, grew by 0.5% in June following a revised 0.2% rise in May. These core figures closely track consumer spending trends in GDP calculations. Despite the rebound, economic analysts, including Wells Fargo’s Sam Bullard, note signs of moderation in consumer spending, indicating potential pressure on household sectors moving forward. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/us-retail-sales-beat-expectations-june-2025-07-17/?utm_source=openai))

International travelers can now use foreign credit cards on China's biggest payment apps, Alipay and WeChat Pay. Starting in July 2023, both platforms began allowing users to link Visa, Mastercard, and other international cards to their accounts, enabling seamless transactions across millions of merchants in China. This development aims to simplify payments for visitors and boost the country's tourism industry. ([cnn.com](https://www.cnn.com/2023/07/21/tech/china-alipay-wechat-pay-international-credit-cards-intl-hnk/index.html/?utm_source=openai))

Alipay and WeChat Pay have implemented these changes by updating their systems to accept foreign credit cards directly. Users can now link their international cards to the apps, allowing them to make payments without the need for a Chinese bank account. This integration enhances the convenience for international visitors navigating China's predominantly cashless economy. ([cnn.com](https://www.cnn.com/2023/07/21/tech/china-alipay-wechat-pay-international-credit-cards-intl-hnk/index.html/?utm_source=openai))
